query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident (email, database, vpn) is a common cause of both how it is triaged/routed (treatment) and how long it takes to resolve. Not an intervenable lever itself; adjusting for it is needed. Note the original table already has 'category', so this partly restates named context.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: The affected system influences both assignment/handling and inherent resolution difficulty; a common cause, not a settable treatment.

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: The observed symptom reflects intrinsic incident difficulty affecting resolution time and how it is handled; a pre-treatment common cause, not intervenable.

per_column.name: is_unassigned
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident is left unassigned is an operational, settable lever an actor can change (assign it or not), plausibly affecting resolution time.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether the resolver matches the appropriate group/skill is an assignment decision that can be set, making it an intervenable treatment on resolution time.

per_column.name: is_open_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Being open/unresolved is essentially a restatement of the outcome status (resolution not yet achieved); it is downstream of/definitionally tied to resolution time, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: caller_segment
per_column.rationale: Caller type (end_user vs automated) can influence both routing/handling and resolution duration; a pre-treatment common cause rather than a settable lever.

judge.rationale: The added columns include genuinely intervenable treatments: 'is_unassigned' and 'resolver_match' are assignment decisions an operator can set, directly serving a what-if question about reducing resolution time. Several confounders (incident_category, affected_system, failure_symptom, caller_segment) capture intrinsic incident difficulty and caller type that are common causes of both how an incident is assigned/handled and how long it takes to resolve, and none are named in the query (though 'category'/'assignment_group' exist in the base table, the added semantic-difficulty columns go beyond named context). The set weakens somewhat because 'is_open_unresolved' is essentially a restatement of the outcome rather than a distinct causal variable, and the confounders overlap with fields already present. Overall the intervention framing is satisfied with a moderate-quality confounder set.
